_: The MANAGED subset of ~/.claude/settings.json — the entries the box's mechanical gates depend on, and nothing else. Everything not named here (theme, model, effort, extra allow/ask/deny rules) belongs to whoever uses the box and is never reported as drift. cc-settings is the only reader; install.sh and cc-audit both ask it, so they agree by construction.
_proven: 2026-08-31: a hook row was canonical here for days and never applied to the live file, so the gate it registers never ran once. The audit reported it, but as '27 lines differ', with a theme change weighing the same as a missing gate. Naming the subset is what makes the report actionable.

hooks.why: the four owner gates (merge/deploy, external comms, destructive, secrets). Unapplied, a worker session can merge, deploy and push to the default branch.

a subagent past CC_SUBAGENT_CONTEXT_TOKENS (150k) is refused further calls until it saves its work and returns a report. Unapplied, a subagent's context has no bound and its cache reads grow with the square of its length.
commits and pushes a track's work at the end of every turn. Unapplied, an iteration that ends leaves its changes only in the worktree.
writes an auto-mode classifier refusal of a planning seat to its repo's refusal ledger, which that repo's permission session reads. Unapplied, the refusal reaches nobody unless the owner relays it.

retired.why: its adapter is off (CC_NATIVE_ADAPTER unset), so on every Bash, Agent and Task call it started a process that did nothing. The tool stays. A box that turns the adapter on registers it by hand (PreToolUse, matcher Agent|Task|Bash), and while the flag is 1 check and apply leave that registration alone; apply never adds it.
the same adapter, off: every returning subagent started a process that did nothing. An adapter box registers it by hand, as above.
a declared no-op (cc-scope says so), kept only for a settings file that still named it: one process per prompt for nothing.

_retired: Hook registrations the box used to install and no longer wants, in any matcher. cc-settings check names one still live as stale and apply removes it, unless the row has kept_while KEY and `cc-config get KEY 0` prints 1: then the box has opted back in, and its hand registration is neither stale nor removed. So is a second SPELLING of a managed command ($HOME/bin/x next to /home/<user>/bin/x), which runs the hook twice. A second spelling is stale only where the manifest's own spelling already runs for every tool it names; one that covers a tool the manifest's spelling does not is kept.
_deny: REQUIRED deny rules — the live file may hold more (the owner's own), never fewer. cc-settings reports a missing one and REFUSES to write it: `permissions` is what decides what a session may do, so nothing automatic may edit it. See cc-settings apply.

statusLine.why: the harness's own per-session context/cost, for cc-context to prefer over its transcript estimate (row: statusline-reports-context). Unapplied, cc-context keeps estimating.

_statusLine: A SCALAR entry, not an array like hooks: apply() SETS it only when .statusLine is absent from the live file. An owner who has set their own statusLine command is left alone — cc-settings never overwrites it — and scan() reports that command back (SL_CUSTOM) rather than flagging it as drift.
